dspace-header.title: GeoCCMM Core 1.0.0
dspace-header.description: Fields of the geoccmm schema. Model: https://w3id.org/geoccmm/core/1.0

dc-type.scope_note: Creator identifiers. Optional. One row for each creator with an ORCID, a ROR or an affiliation. Copy the name exactly as it appears in Creators. Parts, separated by semicolons: name; identifier; affiliation; affiliationIdentifier.
Metadata language. Language of the title, abstract and other text in this record.
Version. The data's own version or edition, e.g. 2.1 or 2024.
Last revision. When the data were last changed, as YYYY-MM-DD. Not the date of this record.
Lineage. How the data were made: sources, processing steps and known limits of quality.
INSPIRE theme. The INSPIRE data theme the data belong to.
ISO topic category. The broad ISO 19115 topic that catalogues use for searching.
Research field (FORD). The OECD research field that CCMM requires. Choose the most specific one that fits.

Keywords from a vocabulary. A term from a published vocabulary such as GEMET or EuroVoc, with the vocabulary's title, web address and publication date. Parts, separated by semicolons: term; termIri; vocabulary; vocabularyIri; vocabularyDate.
Bounding box. The area the data cover, in WGS 84 degrees with a decimal point. If the area crosses the 180° meridian, enter two boxes. Parts, separated by semicolons: west; east; south; north.
Place identifiers. Web addresses of the same places in a gazetteer such as RÚIAN, NUTS, GeoNames or Wikidata.
Period covered. The time the data describe, not when they were made. Both dates as YYYY-MM-DD. Parts, separated by semicolons: start; end.

Spatial resolution. Fill in one box per row: the ground distance in metres (10 for a 10 m grid) or the scale denominator (25000 for 1:25 000). Use the same kind in every row. Parts, separated by semicolons: distance; scale.
Coordinate reference system. The coordinate system of the data files as an EPSG web address, e.g. http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/5514 for S-JTSK / Krovak East North.
Spatial representation. How the data store geography: vector features, a grid, a table, or a triangulated network.
Access. Who can get the data. It must agree with the licence and the file permissions.

Limitation on public access. The INSPIRE ground for limiting public access, with a short explanation. Leave it empty for open data; it then means no limitations. Parts, separated by semicolons: code; explanation.
Use conditions and fees. Conditions on top of the licence, such as fees or a requested citation. Leave empty if there are none.

Downloads. One row for each download: a short name, its file format, format version if known, size in bytes, and its direct link if it has one. Parts, separated by semicolons: name; format; formatVersion; bytes; url.
Map or data services. Web services that serve these data, e.g. a WMS. Give the service address, a name and the service type. Parts, separated by semicolons: url; name; protocol.

Related resources. Links to publications, documentation, source data or other versions, each with how it relates to this dataset. A DOI already assigned elsewhere goes here as "Is identical to". Parts, separated by semicolons: identifier; type.

Funding. Who paid for the work: the funder, its ROR or Crossref Funder ID, and the grant number, title and web address if known. Parts, separated by semicolons: funder; funderIdentifier; awardNumber; awardTitle; awardUri.

INSPIRE conformity. Whether the data conform to Commission Regulation (EU) No 1089/2010, with a short explanation. Leave empty if this was not evaluated. Parts, separated by semicolons: degree; explanation.
